chunks: And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala, from Aban, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father used to say: The punishment of the slave is half the punishment of the free person. This report is general, and it is permissible for us to specify it regarding the punishment of adultery, based on the indication of the earlier reports.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment between a slave and a free person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this report from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id to establish the general principle that a slave's hadd punishment is half that of a free person, as stated by Imam al-Sadiq. He then applies the principle of takhsis (specification), noting that while the narration is general, earlier authentic reports specifically limit this halving to the punishment for zina (adultery), distinguishing it from other hadd penalties like drinking. This reflects the Usuli approach of reconciling general texts with specific evidences to derive precise legal rulings.
